From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Q4 closeout: narrative pass, OKR tallies, and retro rollforward

Team —

This is the final pass before I fold the Q4 narrative into the QBR deck next week. Attached: q4_okr_tallies.xlsx (current numeric tallies) and qbr_narrative_v1.md (first draft narrative). Can each of you do two things by EOD today?

1) Confirm numeric OKR scores for your areas in the tally sheet (use the same 0.0–1.0 scale).
2) Provide one short paragraph (2–3 sentences) that explains the score and any mitigating context I should call out in the narrative.

Notes / framing:
- We need to call out the Automation initiative as a partial miss (deliverable slippage + lower-than-expected efficiency gains).
- Highlight the Hosting reliability improvements as a clear win (include latency numbers if available).
- Keep language concise — the exec QBR has limited slide real estate.

I'll consolidate and produce a 'finalized narrative + heatmap' by 4pm so the go-to-deck work can start. If you think any of these are contentious, flag here; if it's quick, reply inline.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: q4_okr_tallies.xlsx (spreadsheet), qbr_narrative_v1.md (markdown)

Thanks Jordan — quick pass from me. I filled in the product/org rows in the spreadsheet with recommended scores and left inline comments for a couple of contributors. High level:

- Product (Vivek): 0.72 — we hit most milestones but delayed two sprints on the Automation backend; quality metrics are good, but impact on unit economics was lower than modeled.
- Serving Reliability: 0.92 — latency p50 down 18%, p95 down 12% vs. prior quarter, customer incidents reduced to 0.4/mo on average. Call this a win.
- Developer Adoption: 0.66 — adoption was strong in startups but lagged in larger accounts; need clearer onboarding playbook for Dedicated.

Context paragraph to use (short): "Product made steady progress on new-serving primitives and improved reliability; however, the Automation workstream missed two scope items which reduced realized cost savings. We will prioritize a compact remediation for Q1 to recover expected throughput gains."

Attaching my detailed comments (vivek_q4_comments.docx) with suggested phrasing for the Exec slide.

—Vivek

VP Product
Redwood Inference

Jordan —

I reviewed the narrative and Vivek's comments. Two asks from my side:

1) Tone down attribution language around "product-led wins" on the opening slide; customers gave a lot of credit to the new pricing experiments — I'd word it as "product + packaging improvements".
2) For Automation, explicitly call out the dependency on third-party infra work that contributed to the delay (we should name the risk and mitigation).

Suggested short paragraph for Automation (paste into the narrative): "Automation efforts delivered several foundational components but did not achieve the projected cost reductions this quarter due to scope changes and a delayed dependency from our infra partner. The team has a prioritized remediation plan for Q1 focused on instrumentation and two high-impact rollout gates."

I also pulled a quick slide-level edit: move the 'Customer Feedback highlights' slide earlier (right after wins) — those quotes strengthen the narrative. Happy to jump on a 15-minute sync if helpful.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized: Q4 narrative + consolidated actions (for QBR deck)

Thanks everyone — consolidated and final below. I pulled the recommended numeric scores into the spreadsheet and incorporated the short paragraphs where provided. Key outputs and asks:

- Final tallies (see q4_okr_tallies.xlsx): Product 0.72, Serving Reliability 0.92, Developer Adoption 0.66, Automation 0.48. I'll publish these as the official scores.

- Narrative decisions:
  * Opening: use "product + packaging" language (Laura)
  * Wins: call out Serving Reliability numbers (p50/p95 gains) as the primary performance win (Vivek / Marcus)
  * Miss: Automation language per Vivek/Laura — include dependency and remediation plan (Q1 focus)
  * Customer color: include two short quotes from Monica's attachment on slide 3

- Attachments merged into drive: qbr_narrative_final.md (I created, see drive link). Heatmap and customer quotes are embedded on the appendix slide.

Action items (owner / due):
- Jordan: finalize QBR slide deck and share draft with execs (Dec 18, morning) — done (drive link).
- Vivek: provide one-line remediation milestone for Automation (due Fri, Dec 17).
- Monica: send two customer quotes and mark heatmap rows green/yellow/red in the sheet (due Thu, Dec 16).
- Marcus: confirm one bullet on the Serving slide about kernel selection improvements (due Thu, Dec 16).

I'll schedule a short dry-run with the panel on Mon Dec 20 (calendar invite sent). If there are objections to the final scores, raise them here by EOD tomorrow, otherwise I'll mark this thread closed and push the narrative into the QBR deck.

Jordan Blake
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
